transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, um… I came in because I’m having a hard time staying on track. Like, I’ll be working on something—say a dashboard I’m supposed to finish—and then one Slack ping, or even a song lyric or some random idea for another project, pulls me away. And then I realize I’ve completely lost the thread of what I was doing.
Do you find that these difficulties with staying focused and finishing tasks also happen in other areas of your life, like at home or in personal projects, or is it mostly at work?

It happens outside of work too, yeah. I’m not really in a regular job right now, but with freelance stuff and personal projects it’s been a problem. I’ve lost a couple small contracts because I didn’t follow through cleanly, and I missed out on a portfolio competition for the same reason. Friends or collaborators still like my ideas, but some of them are hesitant to work with me because they’re not sure I’ll finish things reliably.
When you think back to your childhood, were you often distracted or had trouble finishing tasks, or does this difficulty with staying focused mostly start more recently?

It definitely goes back to childhood. In elementary school, teachers would write comments about me rushing through worksheets, missing or losing track of directions, and talking over other kids during group work. My parents also had to sit next to me during homework because I’d wander off or start doing something else before I finished.
As a child, did you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble staying seated, or did you act without thinking about the consequences?

Yeah, I think so. I was pretty fidgety. Even now, in meetings or portfolio reviews, I’m usually bouncing my leg or clicking a pen, twisting my rings, shifting around in my chair without noticing. Sometimes I only realize I’m doing it when someone looks at me.
Do you feel that these issues with focus and restlessness have caused problems in your daily life, like in school, work, relationships, or other important areas?

Yeah, it has caused problems. I’ve lost a couple of small freelance contracts because I didn’t follow through reliably, and I missed a portfolio competition for the same reason. It’s also affected working with friends or collaborators—like, they might like my ideas, but some are hesitant to count on me to actually finish things cleanly.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, especially around the time you’ve had trouble finishing projects or losing contracts?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve felt frustrated or disappointed when I mess up a project or lose an opportunity, but I don’t know that I’d call it feeling hopeless. I haven’t really noticed losing interest in things I usually like—it’s more like I get stuck or overwhelmed when I’m trying to finish them.
